Artificial sweeteners and weight gain is a very complex relationship. Even in rodents. My sister just did her PhD on this.

There is one irrefutable fact: consuming more artificial sweeteners leads to more weight gain.

Obviously the relationship isn't direct - since there are (more or less) no calories in them.

The most widely accepted causation for the above relationship lies in the brain:

  • Human instinct is hard-wired to want more food constantly
  • Successfully getting food triggers happy feelings ("reward centers" in the brain)
  • Artificial sweeteners over-stimulate these reward centers
  • Brain now needs more stimulation to get the "reward" normally associated with sugar
  • Brain+body now want more sugar constantly

With a strict calories in / calories out diet, you can of course still lose weight, and just as much. But going off your 'gut feeling' - that is - eating a reasonable quantity, until you feel full - sweeteners will mess that up.

And messing that up is a contributing factor to overeating
